environment.timing_context: Shared unpinned host. No task-owned sustained probes during initial validation/environment/pipeline benchmarks; optional activity from other users is unknown.

changes.behavior: Use min/max reductions for exact native float32 contiguous arrays at 8192..4194304 elements, retaining NumPy dispatch and existing small/strided fallback. Large arrays use 262144-element nditer chunks. Compare to a float32 zero so NumPy1.24 signaling-NaN scalar promotion cannot raise at a one-element tail. Reuse owned comparison scratch in-place, release it before allocating the next block, and chunk moderate equally ordered contiguous depth/validity arrays while avoiding iterator copy buffers for moderate strided arrays. Renderer inputs remain read-only; finite/nonnegative and positive-depth mask checks still precede all cache updates.
Add interval-strided depth layout alongside C/F/reversed/mixed layouts, with input generation and hashing outside measured validation time.

limits: All timings use CPU reference workloads on a shared unpinned host, with no neural inference, GPU training, real robot or web delivery. Compare initial/final within each Python/NumPy row; cross-version results also differ in Python and measurement time.

SensorPipeline validation inputs are allocated before tracing; their SHA256 is an input-content checksum. Environment checksums cover public observations/rewards/termination/reset outputs; recording checksums cover decoded episodes. Timing, traced allocation and checksum passes are separate.
Layout, size and NumPy affect gains. Small/strided/mixed cases can be effectively flat; all raw positive and negative measurements are retained.

Complete environment and recording experiments show positive and negative timing changes. No uniform end-to-end acquisition or training throughput improvement is established. Complete environment traced peaks remain essentially flat as images and owned observation copies dominate.
Traced temporary allocation peaks are not process RSS, GPU memory or hard process-memory budgets. Iterator copy buffers still depend on strides and dtype, particularly NumPy1.24.

The sustained sensor probe validates accepted/rejected batches and previous cache preservation; it does not promise rollback on arbitrary interpreter cancellation or allocation failure during cache writes.
FD/Python-thread equality and weakref release apply to tested cases; sampled RSS is not a general leak proof. Optional integration test skips and warnings remain recorded.
